title: Role boundaries & hosting-tier evidence playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines pragmatic role boundaries, policy templates, and evidence automation recipes for the three hosting tiers (hosted, dedicated, private). It's intended to help product, infra, and SRE teams implement RBAC v2 rules consistently, produce SIEM-ready audit logs, and ship automated evidence bundles for audits.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: IAM role design, environment-specific access rules, sample policy snippets, audit log schema, SIEM field mapping, and an evidence automation runbook.
- Audience: security engineers, platform engineers (hosting tiers), product engineering leads, and compliance owners.

Design principles (quick):
1) Least privilege by default, explicit escalation paths documented.
2) Clear separation between tenant controls and platform/operator controls.
3) Playbooks must be automatable: evidence artifacts should be produced by CI or scheduled jobs.
4) Consistent audit schema across environments so the SIEM and regression alerts can be uniform.

High-level role categories (RBAC v2):
- Platform-Admin: full control over Redwood infra (not customer data) for SRE & infra.
- Tenant-Admin: customer-facing admin roles (for Dedicated/private tenant owners). Limited to customer scope.
- Service-Operator: runbooks, restarts, scaling actions on compute pools.
- Model-Onboarder: permissions for model uploads, signing, and validations.
- Observability-Reader: dashboards, traces, tokenized cost views (read-only).
- Evidence-Auditor: only allowed to fetch packaged evidence bundles (read-only).
- Emergency-Escalation: temporary, short-lived entitlements (timeboxed).

Role matrix by hosting tier (permissions are descriptive):
- Hosted:
  - Platform-Admin: can configure global routing, billing settings, and cross-tenant failover. Cannot access PII/artifact storage of customers.
  - Tenant-Admin: self-service via the Console for keys, quotas, and model selection. No direct VM/GPU access.
  - Service-Operator: can drain nodes and evict workloads but requires an approval trace for customer-impacting actions.

- Dedicated (customer-dedicated capacity in Redwood cloud):
  - Platform-Admin: manages pool lifecycle and autoscale policies, but customer-specific KMS and audit data is segregated. Access requires JIT and audit flagging.
  - Tenant-Admin: full control within their reserved capacity (model uploads, rollout policies).
  - Service-Operator: can perform maintenance on compute nodes only with recorded runbook steps.

- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Platform-Admin: minimal; often a support-facing role with read-only via controlled proxy. Access is delivered via support tickets and timeboxed credentials.
  - Tenant-Admin: typically customer-controlled. Redwood asserts only telemetry & health check access, with telemetry schema contract.
  - Service-Operator: only where customer consent exists; documented and permitted in onboarding artifact.

Concrete permission mapping (short):
- "model.deploy" -> Model-Onboarder, Tenant-Admin (when in tenant scope), Platform-Admin (hosted/deprecated)
- "pool.modify" -> Platform-Admin, Service-Operator (with approval)
- "audit.read" -> Evidence-Auditor, Platform-Admin
- "kms.access" -> Tenant-Admin (customer-managed), Platform-Admin (only when explicitly granted)

Sample policy templates (high-level pseudocode snippets):
- Hosted: platform-managed, reference: use scoped grants to Console APIs only.
  Example allow statement (pseudo):
  "allow": [
    {"principal":"service:platform-admin","actions":["pool.read","pool.scale","audit.read"]},
    {"principal":"tenant:admin","actions":["model.deploy","model.list","usage.read"]}
  ]

- Dedicated: combine platform and tenant scopes; require attestation for platform actions.
  Example: time-limited platform access via JIT token with "evidence_id" claim that maps to a ticket.

- Private: policy must include an approval_reference and confirm tenant_ownership flag.
  Example: platform-side read-only telemetry endpoint requires whitelist of IPs and an onboarding_artifact_id in the token.

Audit log schema (common across tiers) - required fields (export-friendly):
- event_id (string UUID)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- principal (string: user/service id)
- principal_type (user|service|support)
- action (string: canonical action id, e.g., model.deploy)
- resource (string: canonical resource id)
- resource_type (pool|model|tenant|kms)
- outcome (success|failure|denied)
- actor_ip (ip or empty)
- env_tier (hosted|dedicated|private)
- request_id (trace id)
- approval_reference (optional string)
- evidence_bundle_id (optional string)
- raw_request (redacted string)
Notes: do not log secrets, keys, or full request payloads. Use deterministic redaction for PII fields and keep a redaction_version header on each event.

SIEM export mapping (Elastic/Kafka-friendly)
- index: redwood-audit-%{+YYYY.MM.dd} (daily)
- document fields map one-to-one with the audit schema above.
- enrichment: geoip for actor_ip, lookup for principal -> org_id, and env_tier derived tag.
- retention guidance: 400 days for security events, 7 years for compliance-critical events (packaged evidence should reference long-term storage object keys).

Evidence bundle format (for automatic evidence shipping):
- Bundle manifest (YAML-like text) with fields: evidence_bundle_id, created_at, generated_by (CI/job id), environment, roles_in_scope, artifacts: [audit_events_file, policy_snapshot, k8s_resource_list(optional), support_ticket_snapshot(optional)].
- Packaging: tar.gz with manifest + artifacts. Hash manifest and store in long-term bucket with kms-wrapped key.

Evidence automation runbook (recommended minimum implementation):
1) Trigger: scheduled job (daily) and an on-demand audit job (pre-audit).
2) Scope discovery: use current RBAC registry to list principals and effective grants for the target tenant/pool.
3) Collect audit events for time window T (default 90d) by filter env_tier and impacted resources.
4) Snapshot relevant policy sources (IAM registry, Terraform state, Console feature flags).
5) Run deterministic PII redaction and attach redaction_version to manifest.
6) Create evidence bundle, compute sha256, store in long-term bucket (path: /evidence/{env_tier}/{bundle_id}.tar.gz).
7) Emit audit event that an evidence bundle was produced (auditor=automation-job, evidence_bundle_id=...).
8) If the bundle is produced for an attestation (e.g., SOC), upload a pointer to the compliance tracker (Confluence/Jira) and notify stakeholders.

Automation implementation notes:
- Use ephemeral credentials for the collection agent with "evidence-collector" scope.
- Require MFA for manual bundle downloads.
- All automation jobs must write a signed manifest (key stored in HSM) so downloaded bundles can be verified offline.

Runbook: SIEM detection rules to detect dangerous privilege changes
- High-confidence: any granting of Platform-Admin or Emergency-Escalation outside a scheduled maintenance window -> create P1 incident.
- Medium: service account key rotations failing 3x in 24h -> create P2.
- Low: evidence bundle generation failures -> create P3 and notify compliance on-call.

Checklist for onboarding a new tenant into Dedicated/Private:
- Confirm tenant_ownership flag and KMS integration documented.
- Baseline policy snapshot stored in tenant onboarding artifact.
- Evidence automation job scheduled and sample bundle produced & verified.
- Support access pattern agreed (JIT? support-proxy?).
- SIEM enrichment mapping configured for new tenant org_id.

Appendix: common policy snippets (short text examples)
- Timeboxed JIT grant (pseudo-token):
  token = issue_jit(principal="platform-admin", ttl=2h, approval_ticket="TICKET-1234", evidence_bundle_id="eb-20241201-01")

- Redaction policy: fields_to_redact=[user.email, request.body.credit_card, request.body.sensitive_text] redaction_version=2

Open questions / TODOs:
- Finalize retention policy for tenant-requested long-term evidence (customer may require >7 years).
- Automate the cross-check between Terraform state and Console policy snapshot.
- Add a standardized approval workflow (small service) that issues evidence-backed JIT tokens.

Document history:
- 2024-11-05: initial draft by Aisha Patel.
- 2024-12-12: added SIEM mapping and bundle manifest draft (Ravi Singh).
- 2025-02-12: clarified private deployment support access model (Sofia Martinez).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working playbook: prioritize sections labeled "must implement" for Dedicated customer onboarding.
- Link implementation PRs back into linked_artifacts.
